title: Counter Wraparound Visualizer
description: A circular counter dial with draggable start and end markers beside side-by-side naive and masked subtraction panels, on a 10-bit demo counter.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Benchmarking
Embedded Systems

educational.topic: Cycle counter wraparound and masked subtraction
learningObjectives: Apply masked subtraction to compute elapsed cycles across a wrap
Explain why the mask works only for power-of-two ranges

simulationModel.modelType: Modular arithmetic on a power-of-two range
assumptions: 10-bit demo counter standing in for 32-bit CYCCNT
At most one wrap between start and end
limitations: Cannot detect more than one wraparound; a measurement longer than the full counter period is ambiguous under any formula

keyQuestions: Why does the mask work only when the range is a power of two?
Why does C with uint32_t need no explicit mask but Python does?
commonMisconceptions: That a negative elapsed time indicates a broken counter
That naive subtraction is safe because it usually works
assessmentOpportunities: Recover the true elapsed count from a reported negative value
